newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's state miner takes offers for Yauliyacu.
newsitem.headline: Peru's state miner takes offers for Yauliyacu.

text.p: Peru's state mining company Centromin formally received Monday offers from four foreign companies and one local firm for the auction of its polymetallic unit Empresa Minera Yauliyacu.
The winner of the sale, which has a base price of $8 million, will be announced on Friday.

Centromin said in a statement the bidders for Yauliyacu were Pan American Silver Corp, from Canada, Sunshine Mining and Refining Company, from the United States, Glencore International AG, from Switzerland, Paranapanema SA, from Brazil, and Compania Minera Casapalca, from Peru.
It did not give financial details of the offers.
Yauliyaca, based in the province of Huarochiri, 75 miles (120 km) east of Lima, includes an underground mine and a concentrating plant with capacity to treat 979,000 tonnes of mineral per year.

In addition to the purchase price, the winner of the auction will also have to invest a minimum of $15 million over five years, as well as assume an additional cost of $4.05 million over two years to treat abandoned deposits.
According to Centromin, the unit has proven and probable reserves of silver, zinc, lead and copper totalling 7.3 million tonnes. Potential reserves total 14.7 million tonnes.
In 1995, 746,000 tonnes of mineral were extracted from the site.
The sale is part of Centromin's ongoing privatization process.
